sectors.trend: Iron ore crash confirmed; major negative for iron ore majors. However, exploration activity in tin-tungsten, gold, and battery-grade graphite remains robust, supporting junior miners.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face downward earnings revision risk. Junior explorers (FOR.AX, PLC.AX, SRY.AX) benefit from capital rotation into discovery-stage names. Diversified miners with copper/gold exposure relatively insulated.

sectors.trend: Oil spike provides near-term support to upstream names. Australia approaching energy inflection point with data centre demand and renewables transition. Fuel excise cut pressure on government.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, STO.AX, WEL.AX benefit from oil spike. QAN.AX and consumer transport hit by fuel costs. Data centre generator restrictions (headlines 5) signal grid strain, supporting renewable developers.

sectors.trend: RBA inflation fury and Fed meeting focus create rate uncertainty. Housing market weakness (no spring bounce, falling prices) pressures NIM and credit growth. Private hospital operator breakup adds M&A activity.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate cuts vs. housing softness. Healthcare M&A (headlines 39) creates consolidation opportunities. Watch credit cycle deterioration.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup via lender-backed consortium signals sector restructuring. Bird flu in Australian sea lion adds biosecurity risk.
sectors.implications: Consolidation in private healthcare (ADH.AX, IAG.AX exposure). CSL.AX relatively insulated but biosecurity headlines add sentiment risk. M&A activity in hospital operators creates near-term volatility.

sectors.trend: Fuel price blowout and inflation fury squeeze household budgets. Housing market in sustained correction with no spring bounce. Young homeowners accepting lower prices. Retail under pressure (coffeehouse Chapter 11).
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX consumer exposure pressured. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and rental pressure. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) relatively resilient but margin compression likely.

sectors.trend: Global AI volatility (Trump rhetoric, tech chief warnings, Nasdaq selloff) creates risk-off sentiment. ASX tech names limited but global beta drag persists. Steel industry structural decline (Whyalla).
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure minimal but global correlation drags ^AXJO. Steel/industrial names under structural pressure. AI infrastructure spend (headlines 55-67) supports long-term capex but near-term volatility high.

Overweight energy upstream; underweight airlines and transport. Monitor RBA response to fuel-driven CPI.
Reduce REIT and home-loan-heavy bank exposure. Monitor auction clearance rates and RBA mortgage data.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower. Iron ore crash and oil spike create sector divergence. Fed meeting and RBA inflation commentary dominate. Global tech selloff from AI/war tensions caps upside. Expect ^AXJO to trade 1-2% below recent highs. Fuel excise cut debate adds political noise.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Iron ore structural demand shift (China pivot, EV transition) pressures materials. Housing correction may extend 6-9 months. Energy transition and mining exploration provide pockets of opportunity. Immigration policy shift could create labour supply constraints supporting wages but pressuring productivity. AI capex cycle remains intact but volatile.
